items.prompt: A new custom hook is used only by the discussions feature. Where does Bulletproof React put it?
items.answer: Inside features/discussions, not in the shared src/hooks folder
distractors: In src/hooks, so that another feature can reuse it later on
In src/lib, next to the preconfigured library clients
In app/routes, beside the page that shows discussions
items.explanation: components/, hooks/ and utils/ at the top level mean shared across features. Code used by one feature lives inside that feature and is promoted only when a second feature needs it.

items.prompt: The discussion page must show one discussion together with its comments. Where are the two features combined?
items.answer: In the app-layer route, which imports from both features
distractors: Inside features/discussions, which imports the comments UI
In a shared components wrapper that both features import
In features/comments, which imports the DiscussionView itself
items.explanation: Features may not import each other, so the route file under app/routes imports DiscussionView from discussions and Comments from comments and composes them.

items.prompt: In .eslintrc.cjs, what does the zone { target: "./src/features/auth", from: "./src/features", except: ["./auth"] } mean?
items.answer: Files in features/auth cannot import other features, except auth
distractors: Other features cannot import anything that lives in features/auth
features/auth may be imported only by the auth route files
Files in features/auth may import every feature except auth
items.explanation: target is the code being protected (the importing files), from is what it may not import, and except carves out its own folder. So auth files cannot reach into other feature folders.

items.prompt: A file in src/lib adds an import from src/features/users. What does the lint configuration say about that?
items.answer: It is an error, because shared modules may not import features
distractors: It is allowed, because only feature-to-feature imports are banned
It is a warning, because one-way rules are set to warn, not error
It is allowed, provided the import goes through a barrel index.ts
items.explanation: The last zone protects components, hooks, lib, types and utils from importing ./src/features or ./src/app, and the whole rule is set to "error".

items.prompt: Why does the guide tell you to import feature files directly instead of through an index.ts barrel file?
items.answer: Barrel files break tree-shaking in Vite and slow the build down
distractors: Barrel files are blocked by the import/no-restricted-paths lint rule
TypeScript cannot resolve the @/ alias through an index file
Barrel files force the features to share a single api folder
items.explanation: Barrels used to be the recommended public API of a feature, but they defeat Vite's tree-shaking and slow builds, so files are imported by full path, for example @/features/discussions/api/get-discussions.

items.prompt: A component calls api.get("/discussions") and the request succeeds. What does that promise resolve to?
items.answer: The response body, unwrapped by the response interceptor
distractors: The full axios response object, so callers read res.data
A react-query result object with data and isLoading flags
A Zod-parsed object that is checked against Discussion
items.explanation: The success handler of api.interceptors.response returns response.data, so every caller gets the payload directly.

items.prompt: An API request fails with HTTP status 401. What does the shared response interceptor do?
items.answer: Shows an error toast, sends the browser to login, then rejects
distractors: Retries once with a refreshed token, and then rejects
Redirects to login silently, showing no toast for a 401
Resolves with null so that the calling code can show a login form
items.explanation: The error handler first adds an error notification for every failure, then for status 401 sets window.location.href to the login path, and finally returns Promise.reject(error).

items.prompt: On a 401, which value does api-client.ts put into the login link's redirectTo?
items.answer: window.location.pathname, since its new URLSearchParams() is empty
distractors: The redirectTo query parameter taken from the current page URL
The full current URL, including its query string and its hash
The dashboard path, which is the default page after a login
items.explanation: searchParams is new URLSearchParams() with no argument, so searchParams.get("redirectTo") is always null and the fallback window.location.pathname is used. The query string of the page is not kept. The guide elides these lines as "// ...".

items.prompt: useCreateDiscussion invalidates ["discussions"]. The list page has cached its data under ["discussions", { page: 2 }]. Is that entry marked stale?
items.answer: Yes, invalidation matches every key that begins with discussions
distractors: No, the call invalidates only an exact ["discussions"] entry
Only if the hook passes exact: false, which this one does not
No, page keys refresh when the user moves to a different page later
items.explanation: invalidateQueries matches query keys by prefix unless exact: true is given, so ["discussions", { page: 2 }] is invalidated by ["discussions"]. exact: false is the default and need not be passed.

items.prompt: A screen passes mutationConfig.onSuccess to close its modal. When does that callback run, relative to the invalidation?
items.answer: Right after the shared hook has called invalidateQueries
distractors: Instead of the invalidation, because the caller config wins
Before the invalidation, because restConfig is spread last
Not at all, because the shared hook drops caller callbacks
items.explanation: The hook destructures onSuccess out of mutationConfig, so restConfig no longer contains it. Its own onSuccess calls invalidateQueries and then onSuccess?.(...args).

items.prompt: This app has exactly one global Zustand store. What state does it hold?
items.answer: The queue of notification toasts shown to the user
distractors: The list of discussions fetched from the API server
The page number currently shown in discussions
The field values of the create-discussion form
items.explanation: notifications-store.ts is the only file that imports create from zustand. Server data lives in react-query, the page in the URL, and form values in react-hook-form.

items.prompt: A user on page 2 of the discussions list refreshes the browser. Why does the list stay on page 2?
items.answer: The page number is read from the URL search params
distractors: react-query saves the last page into localStorage
The Zustand store restores the page after a reload
The router caches component state across reloads
items.explanation: discussions-list.tsx reads page with useSearchParams() (+(searchParams.get("page") || 1)), so the page survives a refresh because it is part of the address.

items.front: Name the five kinds of state and the tool this app uses for each.
items.back: Component state: useState/useReducer. Application state: a small Zustand store (notifications). Server cache state: react-query. Form state: react-hook-form + Zod. URL state: the router (path and search params).

items.front: What three parts does every endpoint file in a feature api/ folder contain?
items.back: Types or a Zod schema (with z.infer for the TS type), a fetcher function that calls the shared api client, and a hook wrapping useQuery (via exported queryOptions with a queryKey) or useMutation (with invalidateQueries on success).

items.front: State the two import rules and how they are enforced.
items.back: Rule 1: features do not import from each other; the app layer composes them. Rule 2: imports flow one way, shared to features to app. Both are ESLint errors through import/no-restricted-paths zones in .eslintrc.cjs.
